issues.legal_issue: An ambiguous sovereign grant of a residence made as part of retirement benefits conveyed only a lifetime right of residence, rather than absolute heritable ownership.
material_facts: The ruler granted the house together with a regular pension and an additional monthly pension in recognition of the grantee’s long service and on his retirement.
The grant did not expressly provide that the house would pass to the grantee’s heirs or otherwise clearly create a heritable estate.
The grantee had no issue or near relation when the grant was made and was already residing in the house.
The house grant was linked to the pensionary benefits, whose purpose was to provide maintenance and a comfortable residence during the grantee’s retirement.
issues.conclusion: The grant conferred a limited right of residence for the grantee’s lifetime, not absolute heritable ownership.
issues.legal_principle: A sovereign grant is construed, where two interpretations are possible, in the manner most favourable to the sovereign. The document must be read as a whole, and its occasion and surrounding circumstances may be considered as aids to construction. The Court relied on Halsbury’s Laws of England, 3rd ed., paragraphs 669–670, and applied principles found in Raja Rajinder Chand v. Sukhi; Gulabdas Jivandas v. Collector of Surat; Sheikh Sultan Sani v. Shekh Ajmoddin; Azziz-un-nissa v. Tasadduq Husain Khan; and Ram Narayan Singh v. Ram Saran Lal.

rule.if: sovereign_grant_dispute and grant_language_lacks_clear_heritable_terms and grant_links_house_to_lifetime_retirement_benefits and (grantee_had_no_issue_or_near_relation or grantee_already_resided_in_house)

predicates.sovereign_grant_dispute: The dispute concerns the construction of a grant made by a sovereign ruler to a subject.
predicates.grant_language_lacks_clear_heritable_ter: The grant does not clearly state that the property is heritable or passes to the grantee’s heirs.
predicates.grant_links_house_to_lifetime_retirement: The grant links the house with retirement benefits intended to support the grantee during retirement.
predicates.grantee_had_no_issue_or_near_relation: The grantee had no issue or near relation when the grant was made.
predicates.grantee_already_resided_in_house: The grantee was already residing in the house when it was granted.
predicates.grant_creates_only_lifetime_residence_in: The grant gives the grantee only a lifetime right of residence.

issues.definition: When a sovereign grant links a house to lifetime retirement benefits, lacks clear heritable terms, and either the grantee had no issue or near relation or was already residing there, the grant gives only a lifetime right of residence.

issues.legal_issue: A sovereign ruler’s grant to a subject in recognition of service and retirement is not construed as a Muslim-law hiba merely because the ruler and grantee are Muslims.
material_facts: The grant was made by an absolute ruler to a subject in recognition of long and meritorious service on the subject’s retirement.
The grant formed part of a set of retirement benefits that included pensions and the house.
issues.conclusion: The grant was a sovereign grant, not a hiba made under Mohammedan Law.
issues.legal_principle: The character of the grant is determined by its nature and context as a sovereign disposition, rather than by the religious identity of the grantor and grantee. The Court referred to Sardar Nawazish Ali Khan v. Sardar Ali Raza, while observing that a time-limited interest in the usufruct is not necessarily repugnant to Muslim law.

predicates.sovereign_grant_to_subject: An absolute ruler made the grant to a subject.
predicates.grant_made_for_service_and_retirement: The ruler made the grant in recognition of the subject’s service on retirement.
predicates.grant_is_treated_as_sovereign_grant_not_: The grant is construed as a sovereign grant rather than as a Muslim-law hiba.

issues.definition: When an absolute ruler grants property to a subject in recognition of service on retirement, the grant is treated as a sovereign grant rather than as a Muslim-law hiba.

issues.legal_issue: An alternative contention that a grant ceased to be enforceable after resumption or a change of sovereignty cannot be raised for the first time on appeal when it has no foundation in the pleadings or issues.
material_facts: The respondent argued in the Supreme Court that the grant had ended through resumption and was not recognised after the former state’s merger.
The contention had no foundation in the pleadings or in the issues framed in the lower courts.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not allow the alternative contention to be raised for the first time on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to consider a contention raised for the first time on appeal when it had no foundation in the pleadings or the issues; no earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal.
predicates.alternative_contention_not_raised_in_ple: The alternative contention was not set out in the pleadings below.
predicates.alternative_contention_not_in_issues: The alternative contention was not included in the issues framed below.
predicates.alternative_contention_is_not_considered: The court does not consider the alternative contention when it is raised for the first time on appeal.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, an alternative contention absent from both the pleadings and the issues below is not considered for the first time on appeal.
